Title: Diagnosis of test `testContainsNone_StringWithSupplementaryChars`
Details:  
The test `testContainsNone_StringWithSupplementaryChars` from `StringUtilsEqualsIndexOfTest` is checking the behavior of `StringUtils.containsNone` when dealing with supplementary Unicode characters (characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, which are represented in UTF-16 as surrogate pairs).

The assertion at line 381 is `assertEquals(true, StringUtils.containsNone(CharU20000, CharU20001));` where both `CharU20000` and `CharU20001` represent supplementary characters.

We inspected the `containsNone` method of `StringUtils` which has two relevant overloads: one taking a `CharSequence` and a `String` of invalid characters; and the other taking a `CharSequence` and a `char[]` array of invalid characters. The former simply delegates by converting the String to a char array.

The main method `containsNone(CharSequence cs, char[] searchChars)` (lines 1673-1690) iterates over the input `CharSequence` one `char` at a time, and compares each with the elements of the `searchChars` array. If any character matches, it returns false; otherwise true.

The key issue is that supplementary characters are represented by a pair of UTF-16 surrogate `char`s. The current implementation processes the `CharSequence` char by char, not by codepoints. Consequently, it treats surrogates individually, not as combined supplementary characters. Hence, the test that uses `CharU20000`, presumably a String containing a supplementary character, compared against `CharU20001` (also a supplementary character) fails because the method is not correctly detecting these supplementary chars as distinct units, leading to incorrect results.

In other words, the root cause is improper handling of supplementary Unicode characters in the `containsNone` method — it treats surrogate halves as separate chars rather than a single codepoint.

Suggested fix locations would be in the `org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsNone(CharSequence, char[])` and possibly the overload `containsNone(CharSequence, String)` to properly support supplementary characters (likely by iterating over code points instead of chars).

---

Recommended methods to fix:

org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsNone(java.lang.CharSequence, char[])
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsNone(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.String)
